standard_text: The photoelectric effect: the threshold frequency and work function, hf = W₀ + Eₖ(max); the photoelectric effect as evidence for the particle nature of light; atomic absorption and emission spectra; line spectra and energy levels. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 12, Physics: Optical phenomena and properties of materials)

key_sub: Below the threshold frequency, no electrons are emitted.
body_html:
How to think about it

When light of high enough frequency shines on a metal, electrons are emitted (the photoelectric effect). Each photon gives its energy hf to one electron. The work function W₀ is the minimum energy needed to free an electron; the threshold frequency f₀ = W₀/h. Brighter light gives more electrons, but not faster ones.

This could not be explained by the wave model, so it is evidence that light behaves as particles (photons). Atoms absorb or emit photons when electrons move between energy levels: each element has its own line emission spectrum, and dark lines in an absorption spectrum show which wavelengths were absorbed.

Example

A 4 eV photon hits a metal with W₀ = 2,5 eV. Eₖ(max)?

hf − W₀

Answer: 1,5 eV

Example

Brighter light of the same frequency: what happens to Eₖ(max)?

One photon frees one electron.

Answer: it stays the same; more electrons are emitted

Common mistakes

  • Thinking brighter light gives faster electrons.
  • Thinking any light can release electrons.
  • Forgetting to convert eV to J (1 eV = 1,6 × 10⁻¹⁹ J).

faq.q: Why is the photoelectric effect used in solar panels?
faq.a: Light frees electrons in the cell, producing an electric current.

faq.q: How do astronomers know what stars are made of?
faq.a: They compare the lines in starlight with the line spectra of elements.
